method: Exactly two ordinary terminal attempts on http://127.0.0.1:5173/ through existing visible driver, visible briefing/HUD and JPEG inspection only. No source, tests, arranged positions or hidden state. Installed Chrome software WebGL fallback; not hardware certification.

attempts.coverage: Killed induction guard by firing at optic; sprinted west lane, negotiated low cover and recovered west archive. Attempted route out through medical bay and central yard, repeatedly met walls/cover and took substantial damage. Reached east side but died before second recovery.

Killed induction guard, sprinted east lane and recovered east archive. Dashed northwest toward heart and recovered it after correcting receiver position. Tried southwest departure; view stayed near relay while warden filled foreground, health fell from 100/shield60 to 4/shield0 in about three mission seconds. Tried sideways phase and optic fire, killed second enemy, then died.

observations: Title composition, rain, reflective ground, cyan lighting, giant relay and consistent typography establish an attractive cohesive mood. Enemies and furnishings remain visibly simple geometric forms, limiting premium production impression.

Clear mission brief, handbook, paused facility map, numbered recovery boxes, receiver distance and recovered-memory cards make the mission understandable. Death screen preserves score and collected character identities; restored records provide a small narrative reward.

Optic shooting produced an immediately legible critical elimination and score event. Recovery restores supplies and gives a satisfying visible beat. Second attempt improved route efficiency substantially.

Traversal was harder to read than the map suggested. I repeatedly ran against low cover or a wall, with near-identical views after movement. Broad cyan objective markers did not always make the attached receiver location clear; I first approached the visible three-screen console at the heart and moved farther from its receiver.

Threat chevrons and charging labels communicated danger, but multiple directions plus foreground enemies made prioritization difficult. The second attempt's rapid health collapse after heart recovery felt severe; whether blocked movement was enemy collision, geometry, or my input execution is uncertain.

Dash produced visible PHASE EVADE +75 and three recorded evades in attempt two. No confirmed charge-break stagger was observed. Captures occur after driver input release, so sight appearance is not evidence that held ADS failed.
